body:
## Our commitment

ASSERT is committed to making this website accessible, in line with the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA**, and the principles of the European Accessibility Act.

## What we have done

- **Semantic structure** — every page uses landmarks (header, navigation, main, footer), a single main heading and a logical heading order, so screen-reader users can navigate efficiently.
- **Keyboard access** — all navigation, menus and forms can be used with a keyboard. A “Skip to main content” link is the first item on every page, and focus is always clearly visible.
- **Colour and contrast** — text and interactive elements meet WCAG AA contrast ratios. Colour is never the only way information is conveyed.
- **Text alternatives** — informative images have descriptive alternative text; decorative images are hidden from assistive technology.
- **Forms** — every field has a visible label. Errors are listed in a summary at the top of the form, linked to the relevant field and announced to screen readers.
- **Motion** — animations are subtle and are switched off when your device is set to reduce motion.
- **Flexible layout** — the site adapts to any screen size and supports zoom up to 400% without loss of content.
- **Forced colours** — the site remains usable in Windows High Contrast and other forced-colour modes.

## Compatibility

The website is designed to work with recent versions of major browsers and with common assistive technologies, including NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and TalkBack.

## Known limitations

Some older documents or third-party content that we link to may not be fully accessible. If you need information in a different format, please contact us and we will do our best to help.

## Feedback and contact

If you experience any difficulty using this website, or have suggestions to improve its accessibility, please contact us:

- Email: [info@assert.gr](mailto:info@assert.gr)
- Phone: +30 215 555 6984

We aim to respond to accessibility feedback within five working days.
